title: Emergency warning signs
text: Seek emergency medical care immediately for severe trouble breathing, chest pain or pressure, signs of stroke such as face drooping or sudden weakness or speech trouble, unconsciousness, severe allergic reaction with breathing difficulty or swelling of the tongue/throat, uncontrolled bleeding, or suspected overdose. Do not delay emergency care to use an online assistant.

title: Understanding fever
text: Fever is a temporary rise in body temperature and can occur with infections and other conditions. Consider the person's age, measured temperature, duration, and other symptoms. Seek urgent medical advice for a very young infant with a fever, breathing difficulty, confusion, stiff neck, seizure, dehydration, or rapidly worsening symptoms. Use a thermometer and follow clinician or product-label advice; do not give aspirin to children unless specifically directed by a clinician.

title: Hydration and dehydration
text: Water and appropriate fluids help prevent dehydration. Signs can include thirst, dark urine, urinating less, dizziness, and dry mouth. Oral rehydration solution can help replace fluids and salts during diarrhoea or vomiting when used according to package directions. Seek medical care for severe lethargy, confusion, inability to keep fluids down, blood in stool/vomit, or signs of severe dehydration.

title: Medicine safety basics
text: Take medicines only according to the prescription or the product label. Check the active ingredient to avoid accidentally taking two products containing the same medicine. Do not share prescription medicines, change a prescribed dose, or stop a long-term medicine without asking a qualified clinician. Ask a pharmacist or clinician about allergies, pregnancy, kidney/liver conditions, interactions, and uncertainty about a medicine label.

title: Antibiotics
text: Antibiotics treat certain bacterial infections and do not treat viral infections such as common colds or flu. The right medicine and duration depend on the diagnosis and the patient. Use antibiotics only when prescribed, follow the prescriber's directions, and do not use leftovers or someone else's medicine. Contact a clinician for serious side effects or worsening symptoms.

title: Paracetamol / acetaminophen safety
text: Paracetamol (also called acetaminophen) is used for pain and fever. The appropriate dose depends on age, weight, formulation, health conditions, and other medicines. Follow the exact product label or clinician's instructions and do not combine multiple products containing paracetamol. Too much can cause severe liver injury; suspected overdose requires urgent medical or poison-service advice even if the person feels well.

title: Blood pressure basics
text: Blood pressure is recorded as systolic over diastolic pressure, in mmHg. One reading alone may not establish a diagnosis; technique, cuff size, rest, and repeat readings matter. A clinician should interpret readings in context. Extremely high readings with chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness, confusion, or vision/speech changes require emergency assessment.

title: Blood glucose basics
text: Blood glucose results depend on whether the test was fasting, random, or after a meal, and on the lab's units and reference ranges. A single result may not diagnose diabetes; a clinician may consider repeat testing and HbA1c. Low glucose with confusion, seizure, or unconsciousness is an emergency. Interpret a report using its printed units and reference range, and discuss abnormal results with a healthcare professional.

title: Complete blood count (CBC)
text: A complete blood count commonly includes haemoglobin, red blood cell indices, white blood cell count, and platelets. Results can be affected by age, pregnancy, altitude, hydration, medicines, and the lab method. A high or low value does not by itself identify a specific disease. Compare results with the reference interval printed on the report and discuss them with a clinician, especially if symptoms are present.

title: Nutrition basics
text: A balanced eating pattern often includes vegetables and fruits, whole grains, protein sources such as beans, lentils, eggs, fish or other suitable foods, and healthy fats. Individual needs differ with age, activity, pregnancy, allergies, chronic conditions, and culture. Avoid extreme diets and seek professional nutrition advice for medical conditions or significant unintentional weight change.

title: Mental wellbeing and crisis support
text: Stress, anxiety, and low mood can affect sleep, appetite, concentration, and daily life. Helpful general strategies can include regular sleep, physical activity, social support, and speaking with a qualified mental health professional. If someone may harm themselves or another person, or cannot stay safe, seek immediate local emergency help and stay with a trusted person if safe to do so.

title: Reading a prescription
text: A prescription may include a medicine name, strength, dosage form, route, frequency, duration, and prescriber information. Handwriting or image quality can make details uncertain. Never guess an unreadable drug name or dose. Confirm unclear instructions directly with the prescribing clinic or a licensed pharmacist before taking the medicine.

title: Medical report interpretation
text: When explaining a medical report, first identify the test name, result, unit, reference range, and date. Explain what the result generally measures and whether it falls inside the report's stated range, but avoid diagnosing from a single result. Consider symptoms and history with a clinician. If the image or text is unclear, state exactly what cannot be read rather than inferring it.

title: Common cold and flu
text: Colds and flu can cause respiratory symptoms such as cough, sore throat, congestion, fever, or body aches, but symptoms overlap with other illnesses. Rest and fluids may help; medicine choice depends on age and health conditions. Seek medical advice for breathing difficulty, chest pain, dehydration, confusion, persistent or worsening symptoms, or higher-risk patients. Antibiotics do not treat viruses.

title: Allergy warning signs
text: Mild allergy symptoms can include sneezing, itchy eyes, or a limited rash. Swelling of the tongue or throat, breathing difficulty, faintness, or rapidly progressing symptoms may indicate anaphylaxis and require emergency care immediately. Follow an existing emergency action plan and prescribed epinephrine instructions if applicable; do not wait for an online response.

title: Pregnancy medication caution
text: During pregnancy or breastfeeding, medication and supplement safety can differ. Check with an obstetric clinician or pharmacist before starting, stopping, or changing medicines or supplements. Do not assume a product is safe because it is natural or available without a prescription. Urgent symptoms such as heavy bleeding, severe abdominal pain, fainting, or severe breathing difficulty need prompt medical assessment.

title: Sleep health basics
text: Consistent sleep and wake times, a relaxing bedtime routine, a dark quiet room, limiting late caffeine, and regular daytime activity may support sleep. Persistent insomnia, loud snoring with pauses in breathing, severe daytime sleepiness, or sleep problems affecting daily function deserve medical assessment. Sleep needs vary by age and individual circumstances.

title: Diarrhoea and oral rehydration
text: During diarrhoea, replacing fluids and electrolytes is important. Oral rehydration solution should be mixed exactly as directed on the packet using safe water. Seek medical care for blood in stool, severe abdominal pain, high or persistent fever, signs of dehydration, inability to drink, or symptoms in a very young infant. Avoid guessing medicine doses, especially for children.

title: Health data privacy
text: Medical reports and prescriptions can contain sensitive personal information. Before sharing, remove names, addresses, phone numbers, patient IDs, and other identifiers when they are not needed. Share only the minimum information required for an explanation. An AI response can contain errors and should not replace professional review.

title: What SPIRIT-AI can and cannot do
text: SPIRIT-AI provides general healthcare education, can search its included knowledge notes, and can help explain readable text from uploaded documents or images. It cannot confirm a diagnosis, independently verify a prescription, replace a clinician, or guarantee that every answer is correct. It should state uncertainty, avoid inventing missing report values, and recommend professional or emergency care when appropriate.
